ask/one: With queries, keys and values, one token asked: fish. It scored every token's key, its own included, and took a weighted sum of their values.
ask/all: But the tokens cats and like need answers of their own. So let every token ask, all at once. Call the number of tokens T: here, three, each looking at all three.
ask/self: That is why it is called self-attention. In attention over the encoder, the decoder asked and the encoder answered: two different sequences. Here the tokens asking and the tokens answering are the same. The sentence attends to itself.
ask/paper: In 2017, Ashish Vaswani and colleagues at Google built a translation model on it, in a paper called Attention Is All You Need. Their definition: attention relating different positions of a single sequence.
ask/parallel: And they dropped recurrence. A recurrent network reads one token per step, and each step waits for the one before. Here nobody waits: every token asks at the same time.
stack/X: All at once means matrices. Stack the tokens as the rows of one matrix, X: T rows of d numbers, so X is T by d.
stack/Q: Multiply X by the query weights, transposed so the shapes line up, and every token's query comes out at once, as the rows of Q: T by d k.
stack/K: The keys come out the same way, as the rows of K, also T by d k.
stack/V: And the values, as the rows of V.
stack/same: A row stays with its token: row two is fish, in X, Q, K and V alike. Only the lengths differ. A value has its own length, d v, so V is T by d v.
stack/scores: Now one matrix product scores every query against every key: Q times K transpose. T by d k, times d k by T, gives T by T.
stack/grid: That grid is the fans of lines from before. Row i holds token i's scores, so row two, column zero is fish's query dotted with cats' key: how much fish looks at cats.
stack/scale: Then every score is divided by the square root of d k, as before.
mix/softmax: Softmax runs along each row, turning each token's scores into weights: the matrix A. Every row adds up to one. It is how one token splits its attention.
mix/fish: Fish's row gives a half to cats, a quarter to like, and a quarter to itself.
mix/cols: A column need not add up to one. Column zero is how much attention cats gets, and cats gets the most.
mix/out: Then A times V does every token's weighted sum at once. T by T, times T by d v, gives T by d v: one output row per token.
mix/row: Fish's output is row two of A, weighting the rows of V: half of two and zero, a quarter of zero and four, and a quarter of four and four. Together, two and two.
mix/formula: So all of self-attention is one line: softmax of Q K transpose over the square root of d k, times V. A few matrix products, and every token gets its answer at once.
